facts.fact: Southeastern Eversong Woods borders Amani troll country; the patrol sweeps the frontier. Trolls are 'east'.
The ward-stone outer ring lies just south of the troll hollow; a second ring lies further south. Stones follow the border's curve.
From the hollow, a track goes south then east along the ward line; a fork sends the old road north to Silvermoon while the southern track climbs by switchbacks to the Thalassian Pass post.
Silvermoon is a day's ride from the hollow. The Pass is reached at the end of the light after a morning-to-dusk ride.
The Thalassian Pass post is a squat dark tower at the saddle of the pass with a line of outer stones below. South of the wards is Lordaeron.
A high road runs near the Pass; the split-cap stone where Jaina was found stands on the second ring below it.
Snow is in the wind on the heights near the Pass.

Below the outer stones the road runs down switchbacks, then through birch and bracken hills, then into Lordaeron hedge country (hawthorn, bramble) with mud edges and a rutted packed-earth crown. A stream out of a low wet wood runs under the road through a stone culvert.

Farm country (cabbage, beans, turnips, cattle, rowan at gates, Light shrines on gateposts) lies between the hills and Millhaven; farms are long low stone houses set back behind muddy yards. Past them the hedge gives out at a wood of oak and ash with holly.

Millhaven is the first village of any size below the hills, where the road down from the Pass meets the farm roads. It sits in a long shallow fold of land at a crossroads (north road and an east-west road), stream and stone bridge along the bottom, mill by the bridge, inn at the crossing, a few dozen thatched houses; the hill road drops to packed earth then stone at the bottom.
A very deep old leyline runs under the culvert road; lines run in from the north, east and west to the Millhaven crossing.
Jaina came north on foot over the hills by the sheep paths, past heather.

Millhaven's crossing has four roads (north, east, west, south) around a well at the dead middle; the party came in by the north road from the Pass; the road south crosses the stream by the stone bridge (the carter comes up over the hump of the bridge from the south). The east lane runs behind the east-side gardens to a field gate at its top.

North of Millhaven a drove way (the 'cow way') runs from the field gate at the top of the east lane north and a little east, over a shoulder of the hill; it lies two fields and a hedge east of the Pass road, which bends away west while the cut keeps east of north, the two diverging with height. The holly wood of the Ch2 ambush lies on the Pass road. The drove way heads toward the ward-stones, to a stretch of ring between the Pass and the eastern posts that is patrolled once a fortnight by a warden with a lens.

South of the Millhaven bridge the road climbs out of the fold between hawthorn banks into open ploughland and barley stubble, then runs down a long valley toward a line of willows (the river and ford). A gravel stream crossing lies roughly at midday distance; a living farm (rowan at the gate, Light shrine, midden, barn, dog) is passed in the evening on the same day. The ride south from Millhaven is a long day; Chapter 4 opens two days in.
A ford on the river in the valley south of Millhaven has a market (the carter's origin); the carter came 'from the ford, down the valley' that morning.

The sick village lies south of Millhaven on the valley road (the plan says two days' ride; the prose gives no count). It has a cobbled main lane between cottages, a chapel at the top of Chapel Lane (a squat grey Light-house with bell-cote and no bell, a yew in the yard), and below the chapel the bakehouse (brick oven against its end), the long windowless fieldstone granary with a hoist beam, the pound with its stone cage at the foot of Chapel Lane, and a brook at the bottom (the tannery is upstream). Three wells: Cooper's Lane well, a top-farm yard well, and the brook for Ashby's. Cooper's Lane runs down toward the brook with Mother Haw at its end.

Past the brook at the bottom of the village the road splits: north, back toward Millhaven; south and west, the grain road, deep-rutted between hedges, past a ford to Andorhal (three days by cart). The new grain man came 'from the west road'.
Andorhal: 'the big granaries'; everything in the south goes through it. From the village: down the grain road, south and west, past the ford, three days with a cart.
Elsewhere named in Jaina's memory: Boralus (a quay with a flour mill that exploded the winter she was six; a cathedral with a reliquary) and the reefs off Tiragarde (Kul Tiras).

Below the ford the road opens to stubble fields, straight and wide, built for carts; a depot sits where another road crosses it (a dirt junction with a leaning mile-post). Four roads meet there (north, west, south, east); Millhaven is on the north road, the sick village near where the west road bends.

Depot-country places named: Coldwell (past the bridge, further on than Wick), Wick (carters' inn, stable book), Hollow Green (own mill, in no book), Brent's farm (beyond Hollow Green), Elm Ferry (King's road), Ashford (south road, two lanes down from the fork), Brill (north; corn market by the well; Tolliver and Sons), Andorhal, Strahnbrad (up in the hills, on the south road). The Plough is an inn at the halfway point on the river road to the big depot.

The big grain depot on the river road is about a day's ride (noon, if leaving at first light) from the south-road inn; wharf, crane, three barns, a little town with a chapel; the Brill road leaves north through the town: a lord's causeway across water-meadows, then yellow clay hills and a toll-bar.

The fork: the King's road goes straight south-west, wide and drained, into Andorhal by the front gate; the south road bends off between hedges under the hills, climbs past a bridge into the hills, passes Strahnbrad, and reaches Andorhal by the back.

Strahnbrad (Chapter 6, as shown): a huddle of grey roofs where the south road crosses a stream at the foot of a long slope in the hills; Arthas's army camp covers the slope above it, reached by a cut over the shoulder of a hill. The party reaches it in late morning of day 5. The eastern hills across the valley are burning (farms, including the Garrow farm).

The south road after Strahnbrad: nearly empty below the camp, then the flat where farm lanes join and it fills with carts; then orchard walls and barn/shed backs to the road's edge; then a long low rise above Andorhal. They come down out of the hills in the middle of the afternoon.

Andorhal as seen from the rise: a walled city filling a shallow valley, with a granary quarter of tall square timber buildings on stone feet. The south road's gate is the market gate (a militia post just inside on the left, bench outside); at the bottom of the hill carts bear left for the granary yards; a broader straight road to the right is the King's road, running to a bigger gate.
A culvert with a stream running under the road lies on the climb on day 5 morning; mist lies in the road to the horses' knees below it and the road climbs out of the mist on the next bend.

Chapter 7: Andorhal's market gate is a low arch in a chest-high field-stone wall; just inside, carts bear left down a broad lane to the granaries and the militia post is a squat stone house on the left with a bench and a bracket lamp. A carter's yard stands outside the wall where the party's horses are stabled.

Chapter 7: Granary district: Mill Lane runs from the weir bridge to the Corn Exchange (Holt's, Fenner's, the Exchange granary, Garside's on it). Hurdle Lane runs along the backs of the granaries (one wagon wide, in shadow, blind loading lanes every few yards) from behind Holt's, past Garside's back gate, to the rope-walk end of Fenner's yard. Tenter Row (dyers) opens off Hurdle Lane on the right, straight then bending left, with Kett's at its foot reached by a wider street and a long straight back lane. The weir end has the old malt-house Garside leases. Outbound roads: south road, weir road, east road. The weir bridge, the Wheatsheaf tavern, the cooper's door, the mage quarter (Kirin Tor house, inspection offices, sample room) across the city from the post.
Chapter 7: the weather is warm, dry and windless at dusk; dust hangs; no wet streets.
